image_description: A close-up, underwater shot of a large whale's head and upper torso. The skin is textured with mottled grey patterns and lighter patches, consistent with barnacle encrustation. The rostrum is arched, and the eye is visible on the side. The lighting is diffuse blue-green, typical of underwater environments.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a side-profile close-up; the top of the head where blowholes are located is outside the frame or obscured by the angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey coloration with lighter, rough-textured patches indicative of barnacles/cyamids.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only shows the anterior portion (head/shoulders); the dorsal region is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and immediate shoulder area are visible; the full body shape cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint; the visible skin texture matches the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed, and the interior of the mouth where baleen plates reside is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located further back on the body and are not visible in this head-shot crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The close-up resolution allows verification of the rough, bumpy texture associated with callosities/barnacles.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The eye appears somewhat stylized with a perfect spiral/concentric ring pattern that looks more like a graphic design element than a biological eye. The transition between the 'barnacle' patches and the smooth skin has slight smudging/painting artifacts.
Slight excessive softness/bleeding at the boundary of the lower jaw against the water background, typical of AI generation struggling with fine underwater refraction edges.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species identification as Grey Whale based on head shape and skin texture, distinguishing it from Humpback or Right whales.
To analyze the 'spiral' eye artifact and general skin coherence for signs of generative smoothing or pattern repetition.
To check for edge bleeding between the whale and the water, ensuring the subject is a solid object and not melting into the background.

focus_areas: Skin texture coherence (barnacle distribution vs. noise)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the eye. Real whale eyes do not have perfect geometric spiral patterns. This is a strong indicator of AI generation. Also, verify if the 'barnacles' look like distinct organic clusters or just noisy texture maps.
